title: Bitcoin's four-month low near $62,000

lines: bitcoin just hit a four-month low.
Bitcoin slid to about $62,000 this week,
down more than 20% since November began.
Over one weekend, more than $2 billion
in crypto bets were wiped out in liquidations.
The trigger isn't crypto at all — it's the Fed.
Traders now expect a RATE HIKE in December.
A year ago markets bet on cuts. Hot inflation
flipped it — so risky bets like crypto got dumped.
This was a bet on cheap money, not on bitcoin.
Did the rate turn change how you hold crypto?

source_line: Source: The Block & Decrypt market reports, Nov. 2026; CME FedWatch
caption:
Bitcoin just dropped to a four-month low near $62,000 — and the reason has almost nothing to do with crypto.

BTC has fallen more than 20% since the start of November, and over a single weekend more than $2 billion in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated, per market reports from The Block and Decrypt.

The real trigger is the Federal Reserve. A year ago traders were betting on rate cuts; after hot inflation data, CME FedWatch now shows markets leaning toward a rate HIKE at the December meeting. When money gets more expensive, the riskiest bets — crypto first — get sold.

My take: this selloff was a bet on cheap money unwinding, not a verdict on bitcoin itself. The Fed, not the blockchain, is driving the price right now.

Did the turn in rates change how you're holding crypto — if you hold any? 👇
